newsitem.title: UK: STOCKS -- Closing stock market indices, Sept 16.
newsitem.headline: STOCKS -- Closing stock market indices, Sept 16.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Monday.

LONDON - Leading shares hit a new record closing high and set another all-time best as Wall Street strength continued to bolster London markets. But business was, at best, modest as early activity on the back of Friday's surge in U.S. shares quickly faded. The FTSE 100 ended the session 9.3 points higher at 3,977.2, beating Friday's close of 3,967.9.

FRANKFURT - Shares surged to new record highs in bourse and electronic trade, driven by a wave of bullish sentiment after last Friday's jump in the dollar and Wall Street stocks. The DAX index of Germany's leading 30 blue chip shares cruised past the 2,600 threshold for the first time to end the session up 33.91 points, or 1.3 percent, at 2,629.87. Germany's IBIS index of all-day electronic trade pushed higher after the bourse close, ending slightly higher at 2,630.24.

PARIS - Rising bond prices, a stronger franc and record gains on the London and Frankfurt stock markets helped the bourse extend a two-week advance. The blue-chip CAC-40 index finished up 5.82 points, or 0.28 percent, at 2,086.19 after trading in a narrow 14-point range.

ZURICH - Shares lost steam after a firm start, giving up most of the early gains to ended slightly above Friday's closing levels. Strong fundamentals such as favourable interest rates, a strong U.S. dollar and Friday's gains on Wall Street were not enough to offset profit-taking and a lack of follow-through buying. The all-share SPI rose 4.53 points to 2,383.98.
TOKYO - The stock market was closed for a public holiday. It reopens on Tuesday. The key 225-share Nikkei average closed on Friday up 398.71 points or 1.95 percent to close at 20,842.64.

HONG KONG - Stocks staged a strong rally, with the Hang Seng index ending just shy of its 1996 high, as U.S. economic data raised hopes that interest rates would remain steady in the near term. The Hang Seng closed 198.86 points higher at 11,567.90. It hit this year's traded high of 11,600 in February. Turnover was a heavy HK$7.56 billion against HK$5.31 billion on Friday.

SYDNEY - The share market closed higher, aided by the record set on Wall Street on Friday, but the market was unable to hold all of the early gains and brokers expect a quiet week ahead. The All Ordinaries index closed 15.5 points higher at 2,267.8, almost matching Friday's 15.7 point increase, but the index ended off the morning high of 2,275.6.

JOHANNESBURG - A steady stream of futures-related buying of South African heavyweight industrial shares ahead of the expiry of the September futures contract propelled the industrial index higher and marked the day in the bourse's history books with a record number of deals executed. The industrial index ended up almost one percent firmer or up 79.5 points at 8,185.5 hoisting the all-share index 55.9 points better to 6,926.3. Gold ended down 14.1 points at 1,751.3.
